prerequisites: linear systems: impulse response and transfer function

learning_outcomes.text: Study the fundamental techniques of digital and analog communication, including baseband communication and carrier-based communication, covering both digital and analog systems.
Promote qualitative understanding of communication techniques.
Teach quantitative basic techniques for modeling modern communication means.

syllabus_topics: Signals for telecommunication: Deterministic signals and stochastic processes. Fundamental properties of signals and their mathematical representation in both time and frequency domains: Fourier spectra, autocorrelation, ESD, PSD, sampling theorem, Wiener-Khintchine theorem, stationarity, description of Gaussian and white noise.
Analog and digital transmission in baseband: Conversion of analog to digital signals: PAM, PCM, PPM, mu- and A-law, DPCM, DM and MP3.
Signal forms used in the time and frequency domains: line codes and their spectra (unipolar, polar, bipolar, Manchester, etc.).
Required bandwidth, intersymbol interference (ISI, Nyquist criterion, raised-cosine roll-off).
Error probability in digital transmission and minimization of error probability (matched filter, BER).
Analog and digital transmission in a bandpass system: Baseband representation of a bandpass signal (complex envelope), for both deterministic and stochastic signals.
Building blocks for transmitters and receivers: limiters, mixers, envelope detector, frequency and phase detector.
Analog and digital modulation systems: Analog modulation types: signals, spectra, and block diagrams of transmitters/receivers (AM, PM, FM).
Binary, digital modulation types: signals, spectra, and block diagrams (OOK, BPSK, FSK).
Applications mentioned for each topic: analog and digital telephony, radio and television broadcasting, wireless communication, computer communication, etc.
Intersymbol interference, matched filter, bit error rate

assessment_methods.method: Written exam during the examination period

assessment_rules: This is an open-book exam. Allowed materials are: course material (printout of powerpoint slides from VTK), textbook by Couch ('Digital and analog communication systems'), and a calculator. No other documents or electronic devices are permitted.
bibliography: Leon W. Couch II, 'Digital and analog communication systems', Prentice-Hall (current 8th edition)
